decisions.reason: Addressing the same_author_year_siblings flag: row 1631 (paired with blind target_index 52) specifically tests Fischer, Schulz-Hardt, and Frey (2008, JPSP, 94(2), 231-244, Study 4; RPP Study Num 84), distinct from sibling row 1632 (Fischer, Greitemeyer, & Frey, 2008, JPSP, 94(3), 382-395, Study 2; RPP Study Num 86). Note that the shipped DOI (10.1037/0022-3514.94.2.94.2.231) has a duplicated volume/issue segment compared to canonical 10.1037/0022-3514.94.2.231, though original was not requested for row 1631. Although the standalone narrative extraction for Report 79 (https://osf.io/download/5afur/) is blank in the compiled text, the PRIMARY PROJECT DATA record for Study Num 84 documents that K. Ratliff's replication of Study 4 (N = 150) statistically reproduced the original interaction in the same direction (X^2(1, N=150) = 7.10, p = 0.008, d = .46 vs. original X^2(1, N=52) = 13.18, p = 0.001) and recorded a positive replication verdict ('yes'). Both shipped and blind correctly coded 'successful'.

Both shipped and blind identify this exact original paper.

decisions.quote: As far as the relationship between self-regulation resources and confirmation bias that was highlighted by Fischer et al. (2008), we observed that participants with reduced self-regulation resources did not show an increased bias in confirmatory information processing when confronted with participants whose self- regulation resources were not depleted. No difference in confirmatory information processing was found between participants with reduced self-regulation resources and participants whose failure cognitions and negative emotions have been affected by the ego threat. Hence, the present study did not replicate the original results.
decisions.location: Report 80: Replication Report of Fischer, Greitemeyer, and Frey (2008, JPSP, Study 2), Discussion - Summary of Replication Attempt (chunk 849)
decisions.reason: In the primary replication report for Fischer, Greitemeyer, and Frey (2008, Study 2) (Report 80, paired with target_index 53), the author explicitly concludes in the Summary of Replication Attempt that depleted self-regulation resources did not increase confirmatory information processing (F < 1, p > .50) and states: 'Hence, the present study did not replicate the original results.' Both shipped and blind correctly coded the outcome as 'failed'.

decisions.quote: Primary replication Actual Sample 140 psychology students participated in this study for partial course credits. 129 of them were female, 10 were male, and one didn’t report his or her gender. Their mean age was 20.09 years (SD= 2.35). 136 reported being Italians, 3 reported being of other nationalities, and one person did not provide his or her nationality.
decisions.location: Report 80: Replication Report of Fischer, Greitemeyer, and Frey (2008, JPSP, Study 2), Methods - Actual Sample (chunk 846)
decisions.reason: Report 80 (paired with target_index 53) collected new experimental data from a new sample of 140 Italian psychology students at the University of Padua to test the hypothesis from Study 2 of Fischer, Greitemeyer, and Frey (2008). Because it tests the original hypothesis using newly collected data, it is a 'replication'.

decisions.quote: Discussion Summary of Replication Attempt The present replication of Experiment 8 from Murray et al. (2008) replicated some of the components of the original results. There was no evidence that the approach priming had any effect on the present sample. In contrast, evidence (both statistical and anecdotal) supported that the partner criticism manipulation created the desired anxiety. However, on all but one of the original dependent variables, we failed to find an interaction between self-esteem and perceived partner criticism (despite evidence that the criticism manipulation was effective). Our findings did support the original hypothesis that participants with low self-esteem are significantly less willing to provide actual behavioral support to their partners when they perceived higher criticism from their partners as opposed to when they did not perceive that their partners were critical. The inverse pattern was evident for those high in self-esteem.
decisions.location: Report 91: Replicating Murray, Derrick, Leder, & Holmes (2008; Experiment 8), Discussion - Summary of Replication Attempt (chunk 987)
decisions.reason: Shipped coded 'failed' by relying on the RPP aggregate spreadsheet's binary indicator ('Replicate (R)' = 'no'), which only tracked a single focal test statistic on perceived partner disregard (t(68) = -1.124, p = 0.265). However, the individual primary replication report (Report 91 by Sinclair et al., testing Murray, Derrick, Leder, & Holmes, 2008, Experiment 8; target_index 56) tested all six dependent variables from Experiment 8 in confirmatory hierarchical regressions and explicitly reports a mixed/partial overall verdict in its Summary of Replication Attempt: 'The present replication of Experiment 8 from Murray et al. (2008) replicated some of the components of the original results.' Specifically, while approach priming had no effect and the self-esteem x perceived partner criticism interaction failed on most dependent variables, the confirmatory regression on behavioral support provision in the note (B = .301, SE = .145, beta = .357, p = .042, with a marginal three-way interaction p = .054) and exploratory separated support-seeking analyses supported the original hypothesis for low vs. high self-esteem under partner criticism. Under the codebook, this explicit partial replication verdict is 'mixed' (blind_right).
